archetype.name: Game Manager (run-first offense)
archetype.definition: A quarterback whose job in Indianapolis is to keep the league's most efficient run game on schedule with short and intermediate throws. Through five games he hasn't done the core part of that job, which is protecting the ball.

report.headline: The 2025 breakout has evaporated: no deep game, too many giveaways
report.take:
Daniel Jones arrived in Indianapolis and had the best season of his career in 2025. He averaged 8.08 yards per attempt and +0.193 EPA per play, both top-12 marks, and paired them with a positive CPOE. His six Giants seasons mostly sat in the 30s and 40s of the rankings, with 2022 the lone exception. Last year looked like a scheme and supporting cast finally lifting him. Five games into 2026 he has slid back below his Giants baseline. He sits at 5.8 yards per attempt (39th of 43), -0.13 EPA per dropback (35th) and a 1.7% TD rate (40th). He has also given the ball away seven times: four interceptions and three lost fumbles.

The split by depth explains most of it. On short and intermediate throws he has been fine and sometimes good. He has +0.068 EPA on 95 short attempts and +0.467 on 34 throws of 10-19 yards, and the middle of the field has produced +0.419 EPA a play. Everything at the extremes has been a disaster. Throws behind the line are at -0.461 EPA, and screens to Jonathan Taylor have lost value (-0.202 per target). Deep balls have completed 2 of 19 for -0.538 EPA a play, a CPOE of -25.6. The offense still runs at a high level, ranking first in rush EPA. The passing game ranks 29th, because it can neither stretch the field nor turn the free yardage of screens into anything.

What the numbers hide is that this isn't a protection or accuracy collapse. He is pressured on only 15.8% of dropbacks, eighth-lowest in the league. His charted bad-throw rate of 9.7% ranks 10th, in line with his 11-12% marks of the past three years. The deep failure lines up with a gutted receiver room. Alec Pierce, a 43%-snap receiver, played two games before landing on IR. Ashton Dulin and Darius Slayton are out, and Will Mallory is on IR. That leaves Laquon Treadwell absorbing 19 targets. The fumbles (two at Houston, one at Washington) are the kind of thing that clusters rather than persists.

He is also no longer the runner he was. His 14 carries for 25 yards are mostly sneaks and short designed runs, which are efficient (87.5% success) but add no volume. His fantasy floor rests entirely on his arm now. The most likely path from here is a partial correction: deep completion luck evens out somewhat, giveaways slow down, and Pierce's return on Oct. 25 restores a vertical option. That points to a passable starter, not the 2025 version.

strengths.title: Middle-of-field intermediate passing
strengths.body: Between 10 and 19 yards and over the middle, Jones has been genuinely productive, with a success rate above 55% on both cuts. This is the part of the field where the play-action rhythm of a top run game helps most, and it matches the career-best efficiency he showed last season. It should hold as long as the run game keeps linebackers honest.

strengths.title: Clean pocket, controlled ball placement
strengths.body: He is rarely pressured and his charted bad-throw rate ranks in the top quarter. That is consistent with 2022, 2024 and 2025, when he graded among the cleaner throwers. The poor CPOE comes mostly from 19 deep shots to a depleted receiver group, not from spraying routine throws.

strengths.title: Red-zone execution when he gets there
strengths.body: All three of his passing TDs came on 20 red-zone plays, at +0.298 EPA and no interceptions. His short-yardage designed runs add a reliable sneak element on top of that. The low TD rate is a problem of reaching the red zone, not of finishing once there.

concerns.title: Deep game has completely vanished
concerns.body: Two completions on 19 deep attempts is the single biggest drag on his line. It comes with Pierce on IR and two more receivers out, which leaves Treadwell as a featured target. Some of it is small-sample noise and will regress up, but there is no real vertical threat until Pierce returns.

concerns.title: Seven giveaways in five games
concerns.body: Four interceptions and three lost fumbles have undercut an offense that otherwise moves the ball on the ground. The fumbles came in two games and look clustered rather than structural. His interception rate fits a career in which he has typically ranked in the 30s and 40s on picks, so expect it to persist at some level.

concerns.title: Screen game and third downs stall drives
concerns.body: Throws behind the line have lost nearly half a point each, and Taylor's targets have been negative. On third down he converts only 31.3% of the time with 7.1 yards to go, and his average throw lands 1.41 yards short of the sticks. The result is a passing game that bleeds drives in exactly the spots a run-first offense needs it.

trend.note: Game passing EPA has swung from -9.6 to +5.9 to -6.9 to -13.4 to -0.1. The Kansas City shootout was his only clearly positive outing. Week 5 at Pittsburgh showed a more aggressive version, with 11.3 intended air yards and no turnovers on 44 attempts, but that volume came from trailing.

nextGame.headline: Wounded Titans secondary invites shots he hasn't been hitting
nextGame.body:
Tennessee's pass defense ranks 27th in EPA allowed and 31st on deep throws, allowing well over a point per deep attempt. Its WR2s and WR3s have been torched at more than a point per target, the worst marks in the league. That sets up well for Keenan Allen and Treadwell, even with Tyler Warren facing a defense that has held top tight ends 6.4 PPR under their averages, the best mark in the league. The catch is game script. The Titans' offense ranks 31st, opponents run against them more than any defense in the league, and Indianapolis has the best rush EPA. With a seven-point lead in hand the Colts are likelier to lean on Taylor than to let Jones throw 44 times.

Availability on the Tennessee side is what makes the deep game interesting. Safety Amani Hooker (99% of snaps) is out. Safety Kevin Winston Jr. (100%) is questionable after an MRI on his quadriceps. Corner Cor'Dale Flott (87%) is questionable with a chest injury, and Joshua Williams is on IR. On the Colts' side, Pierce stays out until his projected Oct. 25 return, and Dulin, Slayton and Mallory are all listed out. The deep targets remain the weakest part of Jones's supporting cast for one more week.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots vs. a depleted back end
keyMatchups.body: Tennessee's deep EPA allowed is near the bottom of the league, and it may be without both starting safeties. Jones's deep numbers are the worst part of his season. If any matchup lets those 19 attempts regress toward normal, it is this one.

keyMatchups.title: Secondary receivers vs. Titans' depth
keyMatchups.body: The Titans have been shredded by WR2s and WR3s while handling tight ends well. That pushes the ball away from Warren, Jones's most-targeted player, and toward Allen and Treadwell. Neither has been efficient with his targets so far.

keyMatchups.title: Run-heavy script with a lead
keyMatchups.body: Tennessee's offense is 31st in EPA, and teams run against the Titans far more than expected. With the Colts' league-best run game, a lead likely means fewer dropbacks for Jones and more red-zone work for Taylor.

nextGame.watch: Whether the Colts actually take deep shots at the injured Titans safeties early, or settle into a lead and hand the game to Taylor.

restOfSeason.body:
Some of this will correct. Nineteen deep attempts at a 10.5% completion rate and three lost fumbles are the noisiest parts of the line. Both should move toward normal, especially once Pierce returns to give the offense a real vertical receiver. The stable parts are the clean pocket, decent ball placement, productive intermediate work and a top run game. Together they make a competent quarterback, not a liability.

The ceiling is limited, though. He has stopped running for volume, the screen game is a drag, and his career says 2025 was the outlier rather than the new norm. Expect something closer to his 2024 efficiency than his 2025 line: around 6.3 to 6.8 yards per attempt, a TD rate creeping up from 1.7%, and a fantasy output that stays modest without rushing yards.
swingFactors: Pierce's return from the heel injury and restoring a deep target
Whether the fumble and interception pace cools
How often game script lets the run game carry the offense

bets.reason: He has thrown zero or one TD pass in every game (3 in 5). Tennessee ranks 5th in fewest TDs allowed to quarterbacks. A seven-point favorite with the league's best rush EPA should hand red-zone work to the run game.

Tennessee's offense is 31st in EPA and runs well above expectation. The Colts' passing game is 29th and likely to sit on a lead. Indianapolis' 26th-ranked defense and three overs in five games keep this a modest edge.

His two wins came with 143 and 235 yards as the Colts controlled the game. Tennessee sees the league's lowest pass rate relative to normal, and his deep targets are still out. The Titans' bad pass defense and injured secondary keep this from being stronger.

confidence.note: Five games of data, with a receiver room gutted by injuries and a sharp break from his 2025 level.
